'''Martin Gruebele''' (born January 10, 1964, in [[Stuttgart]], Germany)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gruebelegroup.web.illinois.edu/wp-content/uploads/Group_document/MGcv.pdf|title=Martin Gruebele's CV}}</ref> is a German-born [[United States|American]] physical chemist<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/Martin_Gruebele.html|title=Martin Gruebele &#124; Chemistry at Illinois|website=www.chemistry.illinois.edu}}</ref> and [[biophysicist]] who is currently emeritus James R. Eiszner Chair in [[Chemistry]], Professor of [[Physics]], Professor of [[Biophysics]] and [[Computational Biology]] at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name="School of Chemical Sciences at Illinois 2022">{{cite web | title=THE GRUEBELE GROUP | website=School of Chemical Sciences at Illinois | date=11 July 2022 | url=http://www.scs.illinois.edu/mgweb/ | access-date=5 August 2022}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
He was born in Stuttgart, West Germany, son of Helmut Grübele and E. A. Victoria Grübele with two younger siblings Andrea and Philip. He attended the Lycée Français in Vienna, Austria, the Colegio ECOS in Marbella, Spain, and Drew School in San Francisco, US as Valedictorian. He completed his B.S in chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1984, with the University Certificate of Distinction and Department Citation for Highest Honors. He was advised by Ken Sauer (biophysics), Wilhelm Maier (organic synthesis), and [[Richard J. Saykally]] (laser spectroscopy). He did his graduate work at the University of California, Berkeley in the laboratory of Richard J. Saykally, where he was a University Fellow (1984–1986), [[IBM]] Predoctoral Fellow, (1986–1987), and a [[Dow Chemical]] Graduate Fellow (1987–1988). Subsequently he held a postdoctoral position with [[Ahmed Zewail]] at [[California Institute of Technology]],  after which he joined the faculty of the University of Illinois in 1992.<ref name="Department of Chemistry, UIUC">{{cite web | title=Martin Gruebele | website=Department of Chemistry | date=20 August 2025 | url=https://chemistry.illinois.edu/mgruebel | access-date=20 August 2025}}</ref>

==Current positions==
Gruebele, now professor emeritus, was Head of chemistry (2017–2020) and James R. Eiszner Endowed Chair in Chemistry (2008–2024), professor of physics, professor of biophysics and quantitative biology, professor in the Center for Advanced Study, and professor in the Carle-Illinois College of Medicine. He also was a faculty member of the [[Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology|Beckman Institute]] at the University of Illinois, and was an adjunct professor of physics at [[Michigan State University]] to support biological physics faculty mentoring.{{cn|date=January 2023}}

==Research==

His research covers a wide range of areas in [[chemical physics]] and [[biological physics]], including the [[Enzyme kinetics|kinetics]] of biological systems, [[quantum dynamics]] of energy flow within molecules, and optically assisted [[scanning tunneling microscopy]]. A common theme of his research is the implementation of state-of-the-art [[laser]] and [[microscopy]] techniques to interrogate and manipulate complex systems, coupled with quantum or classical simulations. 
He has published over 300 articles, books and patents on topics ranging from [[quantum computing]], to [[RNA]] and [[protein folding]] in the test tube and inside cells, to fish swimming behavioral studies,<ref name="auto"/> and [[ultra-distance cycling]].

==Recent work==
*        High resolution absorption and emission spectroscopy of molecules to study vibrational energy redistribution and develop models of energy flow beyond [[Fermi%27s_Golden_Rule]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://pubs.aip.org/aip/jcp/article-abstract/130/2/024305/922275|title=Regular vibrational state progressions at the dissociation limit of SCCl<sub>2</sub>|first1=Praveen D.|last1=Chowdary|first2=Martin|last2=Gruebele|date=January 12, 2009|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=130 |issue=2 |article-number=024305 |doi=10.1063/1.3038019 |pmid=19154026 |bibcode=2009JChPh.130b4305C |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
*        Dynamics of fast-folding proteins to make the connection between experiment and physics-based computer simulations of [[protein folding]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature01160|title=Absolute comparison of simulated and experimental protein-folding dynamics|first1=Christopher D.|last1=Snow|first2=Houbi|last2=Nguyen|first3=Vijay S.|last3=Pande|first4=Martin|last4=Gruebele|date=November 5, 2002|journal=Nature|volume=420|issue=6911|pages=102–106|via=www.nature.com|doi=10.1038/nature01160|pmid=12422224 |bibcode=2002Natur.420..102S |s2cid=1061159 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
*        FreI (fast relaxation imaging) that combines [[fluorescence microscopy]] and fast [[temperature jump]] or osmotic [[pressure jump]] to study protein dynamics inside living cells and living animals.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://blogs.scientificamerican.com/observations/2010/02/28/scientists-observe-protein-folding-in-living-cells-for-the-first-time/ | title = Scientists observe protein folding in living cells for the first time | website = scientificamerican.com | date = February 28, 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | pmc=6414637 | year=2019 | last1=Feng | first1=R. | last2=Gruebele | first2=M. | last3=Davis | first3=C. M. | title=Quantifying protein dynamics and stability in a living organism | journal=Nature Communications | volume=10 | issue=1 | page=1179 | doi=10.1038/s41467-019-09088-y  | doi-access=free| pmid=30862837 | bibcode=2019NatCo..10.1179F }}</ref>
*       A sub-microsecond pressure jump technique to study fast protein refolding and help guide computer simulations ([[molecular dynamics]]) for how proteins fold.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth.1336|title=Reaching the protein folding speed limit with large, sub-microsecond pressure jumps|first1=Charles|last1=Dumont|first2=Tryggvi|last2=Emilsson|first3=Martin|last3=Gruebele|date=July 5, 2009|journal=Nature Methods|volume=6|issue=7|pages=515–519|via=www.nature.com|doi=10.1038/nmeth.1336|pmid=19483692 |s2cid=21989071 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
* 	With Martina Havenith, kinetic terahertz absorption spectroscopy elucidating the role of long-range interactions of water with biomolecules.<ref>[https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2008/08/080806113314.htm  "Water Is 'Designer Fluid' That Helps Proteins Change Shape" ], www.sciencedaily.com, Aug. 7-2008</ref>
* 	Two-state dynamics recorded on glass surfaces using time-resolved [[scanning tunneling microscopy]], to measure the size and heterogeneous dynamics of cooperatively rearranging regions on a glass.<ref>[http://www.physorg.com/news/2011-06-two-state-dynamics-glassy-silicon.html "Researchers record two-state dynamics in glassy silicon" ], www.physorg.com, June 14-2011</ref>
* 	SMA-STM (single molecule absorption detected by [[scanning tunneling microscopy]]), a technique that can image excited state orbitals of nanostructures with sub-nanometer position resolution <ref>{{Cite journal|title=Ultrafast nanometric imaging of energy flow within and between single carbon dots|date=2021 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2023083118 |last1=Nguyen |first1=Huy A. |last2=Srivastava |first2=Indrajit |last3=Pan |first3=Dipanjan |last4=Gruebele |first4=Martin |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=118 |issue=11 |article-number=e2023083118 |doi-access=free |pmid=33836601 |pmc=7980384 |bibcode=2021PNAS..11823083N }}</ref> and sub-picosecond time resolution.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.illinois.edu/view/6367/295179830|title=Cheap, nontoxic carbon nanodots poised to be quantum dots of the future|first1=Lois|last1=Yoksoulian|website=news.illinois.edu}}</ref>
* 	With [[Stephen A. Boppart|Stephen Boppart]], non-linear interferometric vibrational imaging which produces easy-to-read, color-coded images of tissue, outlining clear tumor boundaries with more than 99% confidence.<ref>[http://www.imaging-git.com/news/nonlinear-interferometric-vibrational-imaging "Nonlinear Interferometric Vibrational Imaging Tissue-imaging Technique"], www.imaging-git.com, Nov. 30-2010</ref>
* 	Computational and theoretical work in the area of quantum energy flow,<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/jp993510s | title=How Does Vibrational Energy Flow Fill the Molecular State Space? | year=1999 | last1=Wong | first1=V. | last2=Gruebele | first2=M. | journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A | volume=103 | issue=49 | page=10664 | bibcode=1999JPCA..10310664W | doi-access=free }}</ref> quantum computation,<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00268970701504335 | doi=10.1080/00268970701504335 | title=Quantum computation with vibrationally excited polyatomic molecules: Effects of rotation, level structure, and field gradients | year=2007 | last1=Weidinger | first1=Daniel | last2=Gruebele | first2=Martin | journal=Molecular Physics | volume=105 | issue=13–14 | pages=1999–2008 | bibcode=2007MolPh.105.1999W | s2cid=122494939 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> and quantum information,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Zhang| first1 = Chenghao| last2 = Wolynes| first2 = Peter G.| last3 = Gruebele| first3 = Martin| title = Quantum information scrambling in molecules| journal = Physical Review A| date = 2022| volume = 105| issue = 3| article-number = 033322| doi = 10.1103/PhysRevA.105.033322| arxiv = 2202.09949| bibcode = 2022PhRvA.105c3322Z}}</ref> as well as fundamental transport theory.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1073/pnas.1600866113 | title=Mechanical approach to chemical transport | year=2016 | last1=Kocherginsky | first1=Nikolai | last2=Gruebele | first2=Martin | journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | volume=113 | issue=40 | pages=11116–11121 | pmid=27647899 | pmc=5056083 | bibcode=2016PNAS..11311116K | doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 	Animal behavior studied by using physics-constrained AI analysis.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1098/rsif.2025.0065 | title=Larval zebrafish swim bouts in three dimensions reveal both new and redundant behaviours | year=2025 | last1=Ravan | first1=Aniket | last2=Chemla | first2=Yann | last3=Gruebele | first3=Martin | journal=Journal of the Royal Society Interface | volume=22 | issue=229 | article-number=20250065 | pmid=40763798 | pmc=12324872 }}</ref>

==Awards==

* 	Gruebele is a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (2013), a Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2010), and a Member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] (2008).
* 	He is a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] (2015), [[American Physical Society]] (2002), and the [[Biophysical Society]] (2005).
* 	Gruebele has received national and international awards, such as the [[Peter Debye Award]] of the [[American Chemical Society]]<ref>[https://cen.acs.org/people/awards/ACS-announces-2026-national-award/103/web/2025/08] "C&E News, ACS Awards, 2026."</ref> (2026), the Hans Neurath Award of the [[Protein Society]]<ref>[https://www.proteinsociety.org/page/protein-society-awards "In 2020, the Hans Neurath Awardee is Professor Martin Gruebele (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191203162612/https://www.proteinsociety.org/page/protein-society-awards |date=2019-12-03 }}(The Protein Society, 2020)</ref> (2020), TREE Award ([[Research Corporation]], 2018)  the [[Nakanishi Prize]]<ref>[https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/nakanishi-prize.html "Martin Gruebele awarded 2017 Nakanishi Prize"] (American Chemical Society, 2017)</ref> (2017), the Raymond and Beverly Sackler Prize<ref>[http://chemistry.illinois.edu/news/Gruebele_Sackler11202008.html "Martin Gruebele has been awarded the 2008 Raymond and Beverly Sackler Prize in the Physical Sciences"], 11/20/2008</ref> in the Physical Sciences ([[Tel Aviv University]], 2008), the [[Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel]]<ref>[http://chemistry.illinois.edu/news/Gruebele_50105.html "U. of I. alumni research scholar Martin Gruebele receives Bessel Prize]",5/1/2005</ref> Prize  ([[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], 2005), and the Coblentz Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.coblentz.org/awards/the-coblentz-award/|title=The Coblentz Award – Molecular Spectroscopy &#124; Coblentz Society}}</ref> ([[Coblentz Society]], 2000). He was also awarded an [[Alfred P. Sloan]] Fellowship (1997), a Cottrell Scholar Award from the [[Research Corporation]]  (1995), the Camille and [[Henri Dreyfus|Henry Dreyfus]] Fellowship  (1998, 1992), a David and Lucile Packard Fellowship ([[Packard Foundation]], 1994),  a National Young Investigator Award (NSF, 1994), and a [[Beckman Fellow]]ship, 1995–1996.<ref name="CAS">{{cite web |title=CAS Fellows Archive |url=https://cas.illinois.edu/archive/cas-fellows-archive/ |website=Center for Advanced Study, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign |access-date=2 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630190002/https://cas.illinois.edu/archive/cas-fellows-archive/ |archive-date=30 June 2018 }}</ref>

Gruebele collaborated with [[Hanoi University of Science]] to port the [[University of Illinois]] Department of Chemistry undergraduate curriculum for Chemistry to [[Vietnam]].<ref>[http://cen.acs.org/articles/88/i22/East-West-Partnership.html "East-West Partnership"], http://cen.acs.org, May 31, 2010</ref> He has been on the list of "Teachers Ranked Excellent by their Students" at Illinois multiple times (most recently before he retired in 2024),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://citl.illinois.edu/citl-101/measurement-evaluation/teaching-evaluation/teaching-evaluations-(ices)/teachers-ranked-as-excellent|title=Teachers Ranked as Excellent|website=citl.illinois.edu}}</ref> and received the School of Chemical Sciences Teaching Excellence Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scs.illinois.edu/news/scs-campus-awardees/scs-teaching-award-recipients|title=SCS Teaching Award Recipients &#124; School of Chemical Sciences at Illinois|website=scs.illinois.edu}}</ref> He is a contributor to [[LibreTexts]], which makes open-access textbooks available to students.

==Personal==
Gruebele is married to [[Nancy Makri]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/Nancy_Makri.html|title=Nancy Makri &#124; Chemistry at Illinois|website=www.chemistry.illinois.edu}}</ref> who is also a professor of chemistry and physics at [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. They have two children, Alexander and Valerie.
He has a strong interest in [[cycling]], [[running]], [[swimming]] and [[triathlon]]<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://wildcardcycling.org/|title=Wild Card Cycling – Central Illinois Premiere Cycling Team}}</ref> and has competed in many long-distance events, such as the [[2013 Boston Marathon]],<ref name="The Daily Illini 2013">{{cite web | title=University affiliates recount Boston Marathon bombings | website=The Daily Illini | date=23 April 2013 | url=https://dailyillini.com/uncategorized/2013/04/23/university-affiliates-recount-boston-marathon-bombings/ | access-date=5 August 2022}}</ref> the 2016 solo [[Race Across America]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raamrace.org/results|title=RESULTS|website=RAAM2022}}</ref> the 2019 [[Badwater Ultramarathon]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://statistik.d-u-v.org/getresultperson.php?runner=866999|title=DUV Ultra Marathon Statistics|website=statistik.d-u-v.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.badwater.com/event/badwater-135/|title = BADWATER 135 &#124; Badwater}}</ref> the 1406 mile DECA 2022 World Championship [[ultratriathlon]],<ref>[https://www.iutasport.com/ultra-triathlon-results/results-2022/results-deca-ultra-triathlon-wc-in-buchs-2022 IUTA DECA 2022 Results]</ref> the 10 day non-stop run at "6 Days in the Dome" in 2024,<ref>[https://my.raceresult.com/295045/#0_3EF1B7 "6 Days in the Dome" results]</ref> 15-Ironman<sup><small>TM</small></sup>-Distances-in-15-Days at "What is the Limit" Garda Lake in 2024,<ref>[https://www.nl-timing.at/_files/ugd/d6d14d_3d6f3a2bedbc44dab16a06ddcbaa1636.pdf "What is the Limit" Results]</ref> and the [[Ironman World Championship]].<ref name="auto1"/> He has written three how-to books on multi-day [[ultra-distance cycling]],  [[ultratriathlon]], and [[ultrarunning]],<ref>[https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D9HX5JL1 Masters Ultraracing Series]</ref> and is an avid scale modeler and pipe organist.
